items.example: This phone is better than my old one.
items.simple: When two things are good, this is the one that is nicer.

items.example: The traffic is worse today.
items.simple: When two things are bad, this is the one that is even less nice.

items.en: A is + adj-er than B: It's bigger than mine.
items.example: My new flat is bigger than my old one.
items.simple: You use this to show two things are not the same. One is bigger, taller or faster.

items.en: more + adj + than: It's more expensive than that one.
items.example: This bag is more expensive than that one.
items.simple: You use this with long words to show which thing has more. One is more beautiful than the other.

items.example: I feel much better today.
items.exampleTr: Bugün kendimi çok daha iyi hissediyorum.
items.simple: Not just a little nicer, but a lot nicer.
items.note: 'much' karşılaştırmayı güçlendirir: much bigger, much easier.

items.en: as + adj + as: It's as good as the old one.
items.example: This café is as good as the other one.
items.simple: Two things are the same. One is not more, not less.

items.en: It's not as good as I thought.
items.example: The film wasn't as good as I thought.
items.simple: You thought it was very good, but it is less good. You feel a little sad.

items.en: the most + adj: It's the most comfortable chair.
items.example: This is the most comfortable chair in the office.
items.simple: Out of many things, this one is number one. It has the most.
items.note: Kısa sıfatlarda: the biggest, the cheapest.

items.example: Our phones are very similar.
items.simple: Two things look or feel almost the same, but not exactly.

items.example: What's the difference between these two?
items.simple: This is what makes two things not the same. One is red, and one is blue.

items.example: Your bag is the same as mine!
items.simple: Two things are not different. They look just like each other.

items.example: Let's compare the prices first.
items.simple: You look at two things and see how they are the same or not.

items.example: I prefer walking to taking the bus.
items.simple: You like one thing more than another thing.

items.en: I prefer X to Y: I prefer tea to coffee.
items.example: I prefer tea to coffee.
items.simple: You choose the first thing. You like it more than the second.

items.en: Which one do you like better?
items.example: Which one do you like better, the red or the blue?
items.exampleTr: Hangisini daha çok beğeniyorsun, kırmızıyı mı maviyi mi?
items.simple: You ask which of two things someone likes more.

items.example: Taking the metro is easier than driving.
items.exampleTr: Metroyla gitmek araba sürmekten daha kolay.
items.simple: This is less hard than another thing. You can do it fast.

items.example: This shop is very convenient for me.
items.exampleTr: Bu dükkan benim için çok elverişli.
items.simple: Nice and easy to use. It is good for you and it helps.

items.example: The food was quite good.
items.simple: A lot, but not too much. More than a little.

items.example: It's a bit more expensive, but it's worth it.
items.simple: You say it costs a little more money.

items.example: This one is slightly bigger.
items.simple: Just a little bit. Not much at all.

items.example: This is my favourite place in the city.
items.simple: The one you like most of all.

items.example: Wow, that's way better than before!
items.exampleTr: Vay, bu öncekinden çok daha iyi!
items.simple: You say this when something new is much, much nicer than the old one.

items.example: The food was just average.
items.simple: Not high, not low. Right in the middle.
